column1: Downpayment for a BTO flat, when signing the Agreement for Lease
HDB Loan: 10% of the purchase price, which can be paid in full using your CPF Ordinary Account (OA), with cash, or with a combination of both. No minimum cash payment is required.
Loan from an FI: 20% of the purchase price, with at least 5-10% payable in cash and the remaining 10-15% payable in cash or your CPF OA savings (depending on Loan-to-Value limit of 75% or 55%).

HDB Loan: Up to 75% of the purchase price for new flat For resale flats, it is 75% of the resale price or market valuation (whichever is lower)
Loan from an FI: Up to 75% of bank evaluation or purchase price (whichever is lower)

HDB Loan: Currently 2.6% per year (pegged at 0.1% above the prevailing CPF OA interest rate)
Loan from an FI: Varies between banks and may change with market conditions

HDB Loan: No penalty if you wish to pay off your loan early Option to refinance your loan with a bank anytime
Loan from an FI: May refinance an FI housing loan with one from another FI or with a different interest rate package, subject to the terms and conditions of the various FIs Not able to refinance to an HDB loan

column1: Conditions to take a second HDB housing loan
HDB Loan: Before you can be granted a second HDB housing loan, you must first use the full CPF refund and part of the cash proceeds^ received from the disposal of your last-owned HDB flat/ private residential property, to pay for your new flat purchase. ^You may keep $25,000 or 50% of the cash proceeds (including the cash deposit received), whichever is greater. HDB will consider the remaining cash proceeds when determining the second HDB loan amount.
